raw_user_query: Explain about the emergence of new dynasties?

orchestrator_output.reformulated_query: Emergence of new dynasties in medieval India and their rise to power
orchestrator_output.text_narration: By the seventh century, existing kings across the Indian subcontinent recognized big landlords and warrior chiefs as their subordinates or Samantas. As these Samantas gained wealth and political power, they declared themselves Maha-samanta or Maha-mandaleshvara and gradually overthrew their overlords to establish independent dynasties. A famous example is the Rashtrakutas in the Deccan, who were initially subordinate to the Chalukyas of Karnataka. In the mid-eighth century, the Rashtrakuta chief Dantidurga performed a ritual called Hiranya-garbha, literally meaning the golden womb, to symbolically transform into a Kshatriya ruler. In other cases, men from non-Kshatriya scholarly families used their military talents to carve out kingdoms, such as Kadamba Mayurasharman in Karnataka and Gurjara-Pratihara Harichandra in Rajasthan. To legitimize their authority, these newly established kings adopted high-sounding titles like Maharaja-adhiraja, meaning great king or overlord, and Tribhuvana-chakravartin, meaning lord of the three worlds.
